what_this_is: The sealed dry run of batch 5, the last: config/m5-phase1b-events.json as pushed in f430640 and still the same in 1c590a9, which holds the thirty-eight attested and pinned events of batches 1 to 4 followed by batch 5's five events in the dry-run state (no attestation). It is the sealed view exactly as the workflow printed it: states, window facts, missing and zero-volume sessions and corporate actions, the thirty-eight pins checked, and no commitment for batch 5 (an unattested event computes no labels). It is the second dry run: the first (run 38735780909) failed and showed only thirty-nine of the forty-three events, as the first_dry_run block says. No label value, price, return, day-1 or gap label exists in it.

run.trigger: workflow_dispatch (event_id all), started by the owner, Fahad9101, from the GitHub Actions page at 2026-10-15T13:30:37Z on commit 1c590a9, the engine fix: the sealed workflow runs only on dispatch or on a push of the events file, and the push of the fix changed neither the events file nor the workflow. The owner's screenshot of the run's page is in the session transcript, line 49053.
run.why: No event returned an error and no pin differed, so the step exited with code 0 (all_ok true in every part).

first_dry_run.failed_step: Fetch real bars and corporate actions and print only the sealed view
first_dry_run.what_was_visible: Ten annotation parts (1/11 to 10/11), all at level failure (all_ok false): thirty-nine of the forty-three events, of which the thirty-eight pinned ones were MAPPED with labels_match_recorded true and REKR was QUARANTINED on FIRST_PUBLIC_TIME_UNVERIFIED, none with an error.
first_dry_run.what_was_not: Part 11/11, which would have held JBSS, SLSN, OKTA and LOVE. Forty-three events needed eleven parts at the 3,300-character budget of nre/event_acquire.py's _annotations, and GitHub keeps only the first ten annotations of a kind per step, so the eleventh was never created. Batches 1 to 4 (thirty-eight events) had fitted in ten parts. all_ok was false and no visible event had an error, so an event in the dropped part errored; which one, and why, was never seen, and the job log was not read.
first_dry_run.fix: Commit 1c590a9, pushed on the owner's word (f430640..1c590a9): _annotations packs the parts to 3,900 characters (forty-three events take nine parts), and the bars request never asks for a day that has not finished (fetch_end: the window's month end or yesterday, whichever is earlier; a window that has ended is asked for as before). LOVE's window ends 2026-10-31, a day that had not come, and the provider's basic plan limits historical bars to data older than fifteen minutes: that was my best guess for the hidden error, and it stays a guess, since the dropped part was never seen (a transient provider error is another possibility).

attested_event_acquisition.read: The Milestone 1 workflow, which watches nre/event_acquire.py, ran on that push; its annotations hold all_ok true for the Milestone 1 events, so their pinned matches hold and the unsealed path is unchanged by the fix.

how_it_was_read: From the check runs' public annotations through the GitHub API (nine sealed parts for this run, ten for the first); the job logs were not read.
findings: All five batch 5 events are QUARANTINED on FIRST_PUBLIC_TIME_UNVERIFIED, as a dry run should be: the provider answered for each, all 21 required sessions are present, and none has zero volume.

JBSS 2026-08-19 lists two cash dividends (ids b819a028-2051-49fd-bcd4-6505d853d06f and ef28820a-6a63-4119-b7eb-0d71f55b7a91), both with ex-date 2026-08-17, two days before its anchor session 2026-08-19: they fall inside no label's window (recomputed from the calendar), so once JBSS is attested no label is suppressed by them. The other four list no corporate action.

LOVE 2026-09-10's window ends 2026-10-31, which had not come on the day of the run; the bars request was capped at yesterday by the fix and all 21 required sessions (the last is 2026-10-07) came back, so nothing about its labels depends on the later days.
The thirty-eight pins of batches 1 to 4 were checked again and all thirty-eight report labels_match_recorded true with the commitments of the earlier runs; nothing about them changed.

With the fix the whole view is visible (forty-three events in nine parts, the longest 3,924 characters) and no event errors. The first dry run's failure (first_dry_run) is explained only in part: the annotation limit hid four events, but what failed among them was never seen.
not_a_claim: Not an attestation of any event.
Not a label, a price or a return: the sealed view holds none, and none was read.
Not a finding that a batch 5 event is eligible: the signoff packet and the owner's attestations come next.
Not a diagnosis of the first dry run's failure: its dropped part was never seen, and this run's success does not show which event failed or why.
